Original Requirements: The I-15 Reversible Lane Control System (RLCS) application software must manage the opening and closing of reversible lanes for peak traffic and special events. It requires five major functions: GUI, Process Control and Monitoring, Sequencing, Data Processing and Security, and Reporting. The system must interface with field hardware (FCU/DCU controllers), support 24/7 operation with 99% uptime, enforce strict safety interlocks to prevent opposite direction lane openings, provide role-based access control, and log all activities for auditing. Data must be updated every 2 seconds, and external systems must access status via a secure one-way interface.
Product Goals: Ensure absolute safety by preventing conflicting lane states (catastrophic risk mitigation)
Maintain 99% yearly uptime with 24/7 availability and rapid failure recovery
Provide intuitive real-time monitoring and control for authorized operators
User Stories: As an Operator, I want to view real-time lane status on a geographic map so I can ensure traffic flow safety.
As an Administrator, I want to configure user access levels and device rules so that only authorized personnel can control devices.
As a Maintenance Staff, I want to view diagnostic logs and device failure alerts so I can identify and fix issues quickly.
As an Operator, I want to execute scheduled opening/closing sequences automatically so that peak traffic is managed without manual intervention.
As an Administrator, I want to generate safety and operation reports so that compliance and system performance can be verified.
Competitive Analysis: Manual Lane Control: High human error risk, no audit trail, labor intensive.
Legacy SCADA Systems: Reliable but often lack modern GUI and external integration capabilities.
Modern ITS Platforms (e.g., Iteris): High feature set, cloud-ready, but potentially higher cost and complexity.
Custom In-House Solutions: Fully tailored to specific roadway needs but high long-term maintenance burden.
Vendor Proprietary Systems (e.g., Siemens): Robust safety features but creates vendor lock-in.
Open Source Traffic Control: Cost-effective but may lack certified safety interlocks for critical infrastructure.
Hybrid Cloud-Edge Systems: Emerging architecture offering scalability but introduces latency concerns for real-time control.

Requirement Analysis: The system is safety-critical with catastrophic risks if opposite lanes open simultaneously. Key requirements include: 1) Safety Interlocks: Multi-layered validation at all control units (FCU/DCU) to prevent conflicting commands. 2) Performance: 2-second status update frequency, 12-second command response time, 99% uptime. 3) Security: Role-based access (Status, Control, Override), password hashing (MD5), and audit logging. 4) Interfaces: Hardware interfaces via I/O drivers, external data export via firewall (one-way), and remote dial-in access. 5) Reliability: Degraded mode support (local control if central fails), redundant capabilities, and non-volatile memory for critical logic. 6) Reporting: COTS reporting tools for historical data, logs must be immutable.
Requirement Pool: Implement multi-layered safety interlocks to prevent opposite direction lane openings under any condition.
Ensure system availability 24/7/365 with automatic failover to degraded mode within 10 minutes.
Enforce role-based access control with secure authentication and immutable audit logging.
Develop GUI with real-time status updates (every 2 seconds) and geographic facility map.
Implement automated sequencing for opening/closing lanes with halt conditions on device failure.
UI Design draft: The GUI will feature a geographic map of the I-15 Reversible Lane facility showing device status (Gates, Lights, Signs) with color-coded indicators (Green=OK, Red=Alarm, Yellow=Override). A top bar will display current System Mode, Time, and Logged-in User. A side panel will provide Control Commands (Open/Close/Override) accessible based on security level. A bottom panel will show active Alarms and Log entries. Configuration screens will allow database table modification for Admins. Diagnostic screens will show sensor-level data for maintenance.
